correctness.rationale: Equation (10) of Zimmaro et al. is reconstructed as F_i=((1+h_i-2h_i u_i)Q_i-(1-h_i)u_i)/2. At any interior stationary point h1>0 and x<=y implies F1=h1*x*(1-x)+(A1/2)*(Q1-x)>0, hence x>y. Exact differentiation gives J row sums a+b=h1(1-x-Q1), c+d=h2(1-y-Q2), and direct parameter partials. Multiplication by -J^{-1} proves both derivatives of P=x-y at every hyperbolic stable equilibrium. Since |h_i|<1, the prefactors are strictly positive and signs follow. The strict rational state (x,y)=(9/10,3/4), g1=g2=1/4, h1=5/28,h2=-2/19 solves both equations exactly; J=[[-109/448,3/28],[5/38,-3/40]], trace=-713/2240, det=1413/340480, derivative1=688/785, derivative2=-1220/471. Exact SymPy identities and rational substitutions passed from the included standalone code. The implicit-function theorem yields nearby attracting equilibria, so the sign strictly entails a finite but sufficiently small positive openness change. This proves no stochastic or global claims.

value.rationale: This is an exact, general sign test for the response of stable interior polarization to separately changing the two community exposures, paired with an explicitly stable, physically realizable rational sign-reversal witness. The source investigates the central science question of whether stronger network segregation increases polarization, and this result exhibits a surprising failure of a universally decreasing openness-to-polarization inference when preferences are asymmetric. It distinguishes targeted community mixing interventions and qualifies source graphical observations by an algebraic boundary. No arbitrary enumeration, trivial normalization, or unsupported global outcome is needed: the criterion applies at all relevant hyperbolic interior equilibria and the strict example establishes an open region of reversed response.
